The HAL_ETH_SetMACFilterConfig function configures the BroadcastFilter field, which maps to bit 5 (BFD, Broadcast Frames Disable) of the MACFFR register. Title: Inconsistent DMA FIFO Error handling in STM32F7 SPI/PPP drivers compared to STM32H7

Body:
Hello ST,

I would like to follow up on an issue that was originally reported by my colleague but for the STM32H7 family here: [STMicroelectronics/stm32h7xx-hal-driver#76](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32h7xx-hal-driver/issues/76).

**Describe the set-up**
- Nucleo-F767ZI
- VS Code, GCC 13.3.1 (inside STM32CubeCLT 1.18.0), CMake, Ninja

metadata.issue_title: Inconsistent DMA FIFO Error handling in STM32F7 SPI/PPP drivers compared to STM32H7

text:
**Describe the bug**
In stm32f7xx_hal_dma.c, the function HAL_DMA_Start_IT unconditionally enables the FIFO Error Interrupt (DMA_IT_FE), even when the DMA is used in Direct Mode (FIFO disabled).
As discussed in the H7 issue mentioned above. In the STM32H7 HAL handles this in the PPP driver error callbacks. For example, in the H7 SPI driver: [stm32h7xx_hal_spi.c L3523](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32h7xx-hal-driver/blob/57ed86b4c358e2333a71fd895b17f1ccdb68739e/Src/stm32h7xx_hal_spi.c#L3487) 
However STM32F7 HAL driver lacks this safeguard. In HAL_DMA_Start_IT, the DMA_IT_FE is unconditionally enabled and the SPI peripheral driver for F7 does not filter this error: [stm32f7xx_hal_spi.c L3375](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32f7xx-hal-driver/blob/e1446fa12ffda80ea1016faf349e45b2047fff12/Src/stm32f7xx_hal_spi.c#L3375).  This leads to triggered error callbacks for a feature that is not even active.

metadata.issue_title: Inconsistent DMA FIFO Error handling in STM32F7 SPI/PPP drivers compared to STM32H7

text:
**Questions:**
1. Could you please let us know if there are any plans to align the F7 drivers with the H7 implementation in the near release?
2. Just out of curiosity, why is this issue being addressed in PPP drivers instead of the DMA driver itself? I am not expert so definitely do not see whole context.

Thank you for your time and have a nice day

BR, Jan

[ALABSTM - 2026-01-14T13:44:08Z]
See also [stm32h7xx-hal-driver#76](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32h7xx-hal-driver/issues/76)

[KRASTM - 2026-01-26T14:15:04Z]
Hello @JohnK1987,

Thank you for highlighting this.

I have shared your point with our team, especially regarding any plans to align the F7 drivers with the H7 implementation. I will keep you updated on any progress.

Regarding the second point, the issue is being addressed within the PPP drivers rather than the DMA driver itself because:

metadata.issue_title: Inconsistent DMA FIFO Error handling in STM32F7 SPI/PPP drivers compared to STM32H7

text:
- The DMA driver is intentionally kept generic and “dumb”, it configures transfers and reports raw DMA status (transfer complete, error bits, etc.), but it does not know how these events should be interpreted for a specific peripheral or mode. That interpretation belongs to the PPP driver (SPI, UART, I2C, etc.), which is protocol‑aware and can decide whether a given DMA error is meaningful, ignorable, or critical in a given configuration.

- Additionally, the same DMA controller is shared by many peripherals. If we change the behavior inside the DMA driver (for example, altering which interrupts are enabled or how some error bits are handled), we implicitly change it for all peripherals and all existing applications using DMA. By addressing the issue in each PPP driver, we can scope the fix only to the affected peripheral and mode, without creating regressions for other peripherals that might rely on the current DMA behavior.

with regards,

With regards,

Body:
I use the latest version of hal_eth.c
compared to previous version there are some modification on PTP related parts and other related to 
HAL_ETH_SetMACFilterConfig e HAL_ETH_GetMACFilterConfig

these differences using the file with FreeRTOS+TCP v4.3.3 cause a problem in dhcp lease..

according to RM0410 page 1825 when pFilterConfig->BroadcastFilter == ENABLE bit should be 1 not

Bit 5 BFD: Broadcast frames disable
When this bit is set, the address filters filter all incoming broadcast frames.
When this bit is reset, the address filters pass all received broadcast frames.

[ASEHSTM - 2025-08-28T13:20:56Z]
Hello @micheledarold,

Thank you for your report.

When bit 5 of the configuration register is set to 1, broadcast packets are disabled, which means the Broadcast Filter is enabled.

Conversely, when the Broadcast Filter is disabled, all broadcast packets should be allowed to pass through without restriction. This behavior is achieved by ensuring that bit 5 is cleared (set to 0) when the Broadcast Filter is disabled.

Title: LL ADC GetTriggerSource() returning zero

Body:
**The set-up**
 * Custom board with STM32F722ZE processor
 * Visual Studio Code, with GNU ARM compiler gcc-arm-none-eabi-9-2019-q4-major
 * stm32f7xx-hal-driver version v1.11.0

**Describe the bug**
I am working on a system that modifies the trigger source of a regular group ADC conversion, in runtime. Using the LowLevel functions in stm32f7xx_ll_adc.h, I can set the trigger source by using:

__STATIC_INLINE void LL_ADC_REG_SetTriggerSource(ADC_TypeDef *ADCx, uint32_t TriggerSource)

I was hoping I could read back the value I set, but that is not the case. Using function:

__STATIC_INLINE uint32_t LL_ADC_REG_GetTriggerSource(ADC_TypeDef *ADCx)

This function returns zero for me. This is before actually starting conversions.

**Additional context**
I found that performing the & operation with ADC_REG_TRIG_SOURCE_MASK seems to delete the exact information I am interested in. See snippet below of this mask.

metadata.issue_title: LL ADC GetTriggerSource() returning zero
LL ADC GetTriggerSource() returning zero

text:
Do I need to have ADC_CR2_EXTEN (trigger edge detection) set at the time of using GetTriggerSource()? That would mean that GetTriggerSource() only gives valid return values after starting conversions using LL_ADC_REG_StartConversionExtTrig(). I would like to be able to r/w the trigger source, irrespective of whether or not conversions are happening. Is that possible?

Thanks in advance.

Comments:
[RJMSTM - 2025-08-04T10:14:48Z]
Hello @FelixBTR,

First, thank you for your contribution,

- The trigger source for regular ADC conversions is determined by the EXTSEL bits in the ADC_CR2 register.

- The trigger edge (rising/falling/both) is controlled by the EXTEN bits in the same register.

The LL_ADC_REG_GetTriggerSource() function applies a mask (ADC_REG_TRIG_SOURCE_MASK) and possibly shifts, because the trigger source is only meaningful when the ADC is configured for an external trigger (when EXTEN is not zero). 
If EXTEN is zero (example: software trigger), the hardware ignores the EXTSEL bits, and the function may return zero or a default value.

The mask and shifts in GetTriggerSource()  are there to abstract the hardware behavior:

metadata.issue_title: LL ADC GetTriggerSource() returning zero

text:
- If the ADC is set for software trigger (EXTEN == 0), the function may return zero, as the trigger source is not relevant.

- If the ADC is set for external trigger, the function extracts the correct bits for the trigger source.

I hope this helps to answer your question. If you have any further questions or need additional assistance, please don’t hesitate to ask.

Thank you!

[FelixBTR - 2025-08-04T11:12:16Z]
Hello @RJMSTM

Thank you for your help and detailed explanation. This explains the behavior I was seeing.
I was hoping I could use the function to read out the configured trigger source. That would have helped me switch between SW and HW initiated conversions in runtime, without reconfiguring the external trigger source. I will now keep track of the set external trigger in another driver and manage it myself. That is fine, but less convenient than using the LL functions directly.

Thanks again. I will close the ticket now.

Body:
**Describe the set-up**
- Bidirectional SPI, high clock frequency, SPI device with FIFO registers (STM manufactured accelerometer)

**Describe the bug**
Function HAL_SPI_Receive generate clock on SPI clock line a few octets too long, for example reading 6 octets generates 9 octets of clock, thus transmissions "with side effect" like for example reading FIFO from accelerometer can result in extremely confusing bugs

Setup bidirectional SPI working at high clock and observe MISO/MOSI line with logic analyzer, use CubeMX autogenerated code.

Hello @KRASTM

I solved the problem by creating a custom SPI driver that manages half-duplex SPI communication without introducing unnecessary SPI clock cycles. I used HAL LL (low layer) routines to configure the SPI and TIM peripherals to the desired states.

The key aspect of the solution is disabling the SPI peripheral within a very strict timing regime. To achieve this, I utilized a high-resolution hardware timer configured in single-pulse mode. The timer is set to trigger an interrupt after a duration equal to the time required for transmitting a single byte * (number of bytes - 0,5). Within the timer interrupt handler, the SPI peripheral is disabled.

The entire read transfer is executed in a "subcritical" section by using the basepri register, ensuring that only the timer interrupt remains enabled during this process.

Title: STM32F723 does not trigger HAL_PCD_DataOutStageCallback for USB Audio on Windows

Body:
Dear STM team,

When I created a new STM32F723ZETx project (FW v1.17.2) with STM32CubeMx and selected USB audio, then it worked nicely on Linux, but AUDIO_PeriodicTC_HS was never called on Windows. I've verified that Windows is sending isochronous audio packets, which means the problem is caused by the STM32 HAL not triggering the appropriate callbacks despite the hardware receiving the data.

My impression is that this line:

https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32f7xx_hal_driver/blob/52bfa97ba66afc08481f6fd7631322593bd89691/Src/stm32f7xx_hal_pcd.c#L1377

is trying to verify that the even/odd flag inside DOEPCTL is matching with the current frame number's parity. If that is the intention, then instead of

((RegVal & (0x1U << 16)) == (hpcd->FrameNumber & 0x1U)))

it should read

(((RegVal & (0x1U << 16)) != 0) == (hpcd->FrameNumber & 0x1U)))

because we want to check if the EONUM bit is set and not check for its absolute value. And, indeed, that small change repairs the HAL_PCD_DataOutStageCallback on Windows :smiley:

Body:
The code for reading data from the NAND Flash in the stm32f7xx_hal_nand.c is *buff = *(uint8_t *)deviceaddress; rather than *(__IO uint8_t *)deviceaddress; which may cause the data always to be the first data read from the nand flash when code is optimized by the compiler.

Title: Bug in CRC32 calculation

Body:
Hi,

On this line:
https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32f7xx_hal_driver/blob/8a83a680a5c0c678df3897ae41b430444abb3cb7/Src/stm32f7xx_hal_crc.c#L453

and on this one too:
https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32f7xx_hal_driver/blob/8a83a680a5c0c678df3897ae41b430444abb3cb7/Src/stm32f7xx_hal_crc.c#L467

it's missing a cast to (uint8_t) when loading the DR register, otherwise it won't compute the correct CRC32.

Comments:
[ALABSTM - 2020-04-16T08:31:22Z]
Hi @josesimoes,

Thank you for your report. May I ask you to provide us with the test case that allowed you to obtain an incorrect CRC32?

Thank you,

[josesimoes - 2020-04-16T08:45:20Z]
@ALABSTM I haven't added any test case… just found out about it when using the code on my app.
The issue is not a specific to a particular calculation is just wrong for any calculation on which there is a single byte left in the buffer (after feeding the register with 32bits data chunks). On another perspective, if one is feeding the calculator with a byte array with an odd length.

[ALABSTM - 2020-04-16T09:31:13Z]
Hi @josesimoes,

metadata.issue_title: Bug in CRC32 calculation

text:
Do you confirm you obtain a wrong CRC32 even though member InputDataFormat in the handler structure is set to CRC_INPUTDATA_FORMAT_BYTES? Thank you in advance for your answer.

With regards,

[josesimoes - 2020-04-16T09:34:11Z]
That is correct. On our project the CRC32 only applies to byte arrays and we set the InputDataFormat to CRC_INPUTDATA_FORMAT_BYTES  when configuring the CRC peripheral. And that is never changed afterwards.

[ALABSTM - 2020-04-16T10:02:42Z]
Hi @josesimoes,

Thank you for your answer. In order to be sure I correctly understood your request, you suggest the following implementation?
diff
- *(__IO uint8_t *)(__IO void *)(&hcrc->Instance->DR) = pBuffer[4U * i];
+ *(__IO uint8_t *)(__IO void *)(&hcrc->Instance->DR) = (uint8_t) pBuffer[4U * i];

May I also ask you whether you obtained a correct CRC once you added the cast? Thank you for your answers once more.

With regards,

[josesimoes - 2020-04-16T10:19:23Z]
Basically yes. On both lines 453 and 467. That cast is all that's needed to fix this. Actually inline with the other casts there on the other data sizes cases.

[ALABSTM - 2020-04-16T10:47:05Z]
Hi @josesimoes,

metadata.issue_title: Bug in CRC32 calculation

text:
Please excuse my insistence. Do you confirm you updated the two lines above by adding the (uint8_t)cast to the pBuffer[4U * i] array element and had the issue fixed in consequence (**i.e.** the correct CRC has been obtained)?

I ask the question because the pBuffer parameter is already defined to be a pointer on uint8_t data. Thank you for your comprehension.

With regards,

[josesimoes - 2020-04-16T12:01:27Z]
Hi again,

That is correct. I agree that this sounds weird but it is what it is... I guess that's probably because of the way the compiler is handling that. The cast makes sure that the proper data and size are feed to the CRC32 register.

All that code feeding the registers looks over engineered and there are notes about that. 
If it's of interest: I'm using GCC 8-2019-q3-update.
